prs.title: feat: support Gitea workflows in .gitea/workflows (#132)
prs.body:
Closes #132

## Problem

Gitea runs GitHub-compatible workflows, but it looks in `.gitea/workflows` first. In a repository that only has that directory:

- `wrkflw validate` failed with `Path does not exist: .github/workflows`.
- `wrkflw list`, the TUI and `wrkflw watch` found nothing by default.
- `actions/checkout` dropped `.gitea` from the workspace, so steps could not read it.
- `${{ gitea.ref }}` silently evaluated to an empty value.

An explicit `wrkflw validate .gitea/workflows` already worked, and the validator already accepted Gitea-style syntax.

## Changes

- **Discovery:** new helpers in `wrkflw-utils` use Gitea's order, `.gitea/workflows` then `.github/workflows`. The order comes from `WorkflowDirs` in Gitea's `modules/setting/actions.go`.
- **`validate`, `list` and the TUI:** these cover both directories when both exist. Gitea only runs the first, but a repository mirrored to both forges uses both.
- **`watch`:** this takes one directory, so it picks `.gitea/workflows` and prints a note naming the skipped one.
- **Workspace copy:** both copy routines now keep `.gitea`.
- **Expressions:** `gitea` is an alias of the `github` context.
- **`list` refactor:** the directory listing moved into `list_workflow_dir`, which accounts for most of the `main.rs` diff.

## Behaviour change

In a repository with both directories, `wrkflw watch` now defaults to `.gitea/workflows`, not `.github/workflows`. Repositories with only `.github/workflows` are unaffected, except that the `list` message is reworded when neither directory exists.

## Not included

- **Absolute-URL actions:** `uses: https://gitea.com/actions/checkout@v4` passes validation, but at run time the URL is mangled and the step falls back to built-in handling, reporting success. This is listed under "Not yet supported" in the README.
- **Remote triggering:** `trigger` stays GitHub and GitLab only.
- **Forgejo:** `.forgejo/workflows` is not discovered.

## Testing

- `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` all pass.
- New unit tests cover directory ordering, both workspace copies and the `gitea` alias.
- I ran the built binary against `.gitea`-only, both-directory and neither-directory repositories for `validate` and `list`, and started `watch` on the first two.
- An emulation run with `actions/checkout` reads `.gitea/workflows/co.yml` with the fix and fails when the engine copy change is reverted.
- The TUI, driven through a pseudo-terminal, lists `.gitea/workflows`, both directories together, and `.github/workflows` alone, and it ran a `.gitea` workflow to success.
- A workflow using `actions/checkout`, a local `.gitea` composite action, `gitea.*` expressions and a reusable `.gitea` workflow passes under the emulation and Podman runtimes. Docker was not running, so it was not tested.
- `wrkflw validate` exits 1 on an invalid `.gitea` workflow, and `wrkflw watch` triggers when a `.gitea` workflow is edited.

## Existing issues found, not caused by this PR

- `secure-emulation` fails the same workflow from `.github`: a step cannot see checked-out files.
- `wrkflw watch` on macOS re-triggers many times after one edit. Unmodified `main` and this branch both logged about 20 detections in 12 seconds.

prs.title: fix(ui): add a light theme for light terminals (#120)
prs.body:
Fixes #120.

## Problem

The TUI palette was hard-coded for dark backgrounds. On a light terminal, pale yellow and cyan text was nearly invisible, and the title bar, status bar and selected row stayed near-black.

## Changes

- **Light palette:** `COLORS` now resolves to a dark or light table at runtime, so existing call sites are unchanged. The dark palette keeps its values.
- **Accents:** each Tweaks accent has a light variant. The accent overrides the palette on every frame, so the palette alone would not have fixed it.
- **Help overlay:** the backdrop uses the theme instead of hard-coded black.
- **Theme selection:** the theme is chosen once at startup, in this order:
  1. `--theme auto|dark|light`
  2. `WRKFLW_THEME`
  3. The terminal's reported background
  4. `COLORFGBG`
  5. Dark

Auto-detection suits terminals that change theme by time of day, as in the issue.

## Notes for review

- **New dependency:** `terminal-colorsaurus` is added behind the `tui` feature. It resolves to 1.0.0 because 1.0.3 conflicts with the `mio` version required by `crossterm` 0.28.
- **Public API:** `run_wrkflw_tui` gains a `theme` parameter, which is a breaking change for library users. The READMEs are updated.
- **Startup delay:** a terminal that answers neither color nor device queries delays startup by up to 1 second. Explicit `--theme dark` or `--theme light` skips the query.
- **No live switching:** changing the terminal theme needs a TUI restart. A live toggle is left out because the log worker caches styles built from the old palette.
- **Forced light on a dark terminal:** the TUI does not paint the main background, so light text colors are the user's explicit choice there.

## Testing

- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --workspace` pass.
- `wrkflw` builds with `--no-default-features`.
- New unit tests require 4.5:1 contrast for light-theme text on white and on every light background, and for solid chips.
- The real binary was run in a scripted pseudo-terminal, reading the colors it emitted:
  - Flag, environment variable, flag precedence and invalid environment values behaved as designed.
  - Simulated white and black terminals selected light and dark.
  - A silent terminal used `COLORFGBG`, then dark.
- This has not been checked by eye in a real terminal emulator.

prs.title: fix: use platform base directories instead of ~/.wrkflw (#117)
prs.body:
Fixes #117.

## Problem

wrkflw hardcoded `~/.wrkflw/` in three places: the `actions/cache` store (the one the issue cites), `RUNNER_TOOL_CACHE`, and the default `file` secrets provider path.

## Changes

| Purpose | Before | Linux | macOS |
|---------|--------|-------|-------|
| `actions/cache` store | `~/.wrkflw/cache` | `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/wrkflw/cache` | `~/Library/Caches/wrkflw/cache` |
| `RUNNER_TOOL_CACHE` | `~/.wrkflw/tools` | `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/wrkflw/tools` | `~/Library/Caches/wrkflw/tools` |
| Default `file` secrets | `~/.wrkflw/secrets` | `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/wrkflw/secrets` | `~/Library/Application Support/wrkflw/secrets` |

Paths come from the `dirs` crate, which was already a dependency, so `$XDG_*` is honoured on Linux and macOS and Windows use their native locations. `$XDG_*` is not read on macOS.

## Migration

- **Secrets:** `~/.wrkflw/secrets` keeps being used until the new location exists, so upgrading does not hide anyone's secrets.
- **Caches:** not migrated, because they repopulate on the next run. The old directories are left in place, and `BREAKING_CHANGES.md` documents how to delete them.

## Testing

- `cargo test --workspace` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass.
- New unit tests cover how the secrets path is chosen (new location, legacy fallback, both present, neither resolvable).
- End-to-end on macOS with an isolated `HOME`: an emulation run saved and then restored an `actions/cache` entry under `Library/Caches/wrkflw/cache`, `RUNNER_TOOL_CACHE` pointed at `Library/Caches/wrkflw/tools`, and no `~/.wrkflw` was created.
- CI passes on Linux, macOS and Windows, but only the macOS paths were exercised end-to-end. The `$XDG_*` lookup on Linux relies on `dirs`.

## Docs

The secrets docs described `~/.wrkflw/secrets.yml` as if it were picked up automatically, but nothing loads a config file by default. The paths are updated, and the root README now points at the secrets directory the `file` provider actually reads. `crates/secrets/README.md` and the secrets demo still describe a config file there and only had their paths changed.

prs.title: feat(matrix): support expressions in matrix include and exclude (#112)
prs.body:
Closes #112

## Problem

`strategy.matrix.include: ${{ fromJSON(needs.<job>.outputs.<name>) }}` is valid GitHub Actions syntax, but `wrkflw validate` failed with `include must be an array of objects`. Fixing that message alone wasn't enough, because `MatrixConfig` couldn't deserialize a string there either.

## Changes

- **`wrkflw-matrix`:** `include` and `exclude` are now `MatrixEntries`, either a literal `List` or an `Expression`. `MatrixConfig::resolve_expressions` turns expressions into lists. `expand_matrix` returns an error if one is still unresolved, rather than silently dropping it.
- **Include-only matrices:** a matrix with `include` and no axes now expands. It used to fail with "Matrix has no valid parameters", and it's a common shape for generated matrices.
- **Strategy contexts:** expressions may use only `github`, `needs`, `vars` and `inputs`, and no special functions, matching GitHub's `strategy` context. `wrkflw validate` and `wrkflw run` share this check. `vars` is accepted but wrkflw does not resolve it, so it evaluates to empty.
- **Executor:** expressions are resolved after the job's `if:` gate. A matrix that can't be computed fails that job, and its dependents are skipped.
- **Validator and parser:** accept a value wrapped in `${{ }}`. Plain strings and non-object items are still rejected.
- **TUI:** the matrix pane shows an expansion error for these jobs, because the combinations aren't known until the run.

## Behaviour to check

- If the expression doesn't evaluate to an array of objects, the job fails and the rest of the run continues. This includes an empty output, and an include-only matrix that resolves to `[]`. Static expansion failures now behave the same way.
- `MatrixConfig.include` and `.exclude` change type, which is a breaking change to the public API of `wrkflw-matrix`.

## Not included

- Expressions for the whole matrix (`matrix: ${{ ... }}`) are still rejected.
- Expressions for a single axis (`os: ${{ ... }}`) still pass validation but are treated as a literal value at run time.

## Testing

- Added unit tests in `wrkflw-matrix` and the validator.
- Added `crates/wrkflw/tests/dynamic_matrix_test.rs`, which runs merging, include-only, exclude and invalid-result cases end to end through emulation.
- `cargo test --workspace` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass.
- Ran a local workflow with the same shape as the issue's, with `list.py` replaced by its hard-coded JSON output and the install and setup-node steps removed. It validated and ran 4 combinations.

prs.title: fix(ui): clear terminal on TUI startup (#111)
prs.body:
Fixes #111.

## Problem
On some terminals (reported on iTerm2), entering the alternate screen keeps whatever was on the primary screen. ratatui assumes the terminal starts blank and only writes cells that change between frames, so pre-existing text stayed visible in any region a frame didn't paint — including after switching tabs such as Logs.

## Fix
Call `terminal.clear()` right after constructing the ratatui `Terminal`. This clears the physical screen and resets ratatui's back buffer, so the first frame is drawn onto a known-empty screen. Resizes are already handled by ratatui's autoresize, which clears too.

## Testing
- `cargo build` / `cargo clippy` / `cargo fmt --check` for `wrkflw-ui`
- Not verified interactively in iTerm2

prs.title: fix(gitlab): resolve include, spec:inputs, extends and hidden jobs
prs.body:
Fixes #109.

## Problem

wrkflw parsed only the top-level `.gitlab-ci.yml`, as written. Real pipelines like the two in the issue failed:

- **rust-json-job-dispatch**: hidden `.`-prefixed templates were reported as jobs with no script, and every `extends` target defined in an `include`d file showed up as `extends undefined job`.
- **ParaView**: failed straight away with `deserializing from YAML containing more than one document is not supported`, because of its `spec:inputs` header.

Even where validation passed, `extends` was never applied, so a job that took its `script` from a template would run with no steps.

## Fix

A new `gitlab_config` module in the parser builds the resolved configuration before it is deserialized into `Pipeline`:

| Feature | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `include` | Local includes, given as a string, as `local:`, or with wildcards. They are deep-merged in order and the including file wins. Cycles are detected, and paths must stay inside the repository. `remote`/`project`/`template`/`component` are **skipped with a warning**, since they need network access. |
| `spec:inputs` | Header document plus `$[[ inputs.x ]]` interpolation in keys and values. Uses defaults and checks `type`/`options`/`regex`. Reports required inputs that are missing and inputs that are unknown. A whole-string placeholder keeps its type (number/bool/array). Supports `expand_vars`, `truncate(a,b)` and `posix_escape`. |
| `extends` | Deep merge, multiple parents applied in order, transitive. Cycle and depth (11) limits. |
| `!reference` | Resolved after `extends`, nesting limited to 10 levels. Nested script arrays (from anchors or references) are flattened, as GitLab does. |
| Hidden keys | `.`-prefixed keys are removed once resolved, so they are never treated as jobs. |

Smaller model and schema gaps that the example pipelines hit:
- `allow_failure: { exit_codes: ... }` is now accepted (new `AllowFailure` enum; the field had no other users).
- Jobs with `trigger:` and no `script` are accepted by the validators.
- The bundled schema now accepts a list for `artifacts:reports:annotations` and null/empty variable values. ParaView uses both and GitLab accepts both.
- Schema errors now include the JSON path (e.g. `/job/variables/FOO: ...`). The merged config has no line numbers, so without the path these errors were impossible to locate.

## Testing

- 12 new unit tests in `gitlab_config` and one `parse_pipeline` integration test. They cover merging, overrides, wildcards, skipped includes, cycles, escaping the repository root, typed inputs, input errors, `!reference`, and anchor flattening.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features -- -D warnings`, `cargo check --no-default-features`, `cargo test --workspace --all-features` all pass locally (853 tests).
- Both pipelines from the issue now validate cleanly (`wrkflw validate .gitlab-ci.yml`). ParaView resolves to 25 jobs across its include/inputs chain.
- End-to-end `wrkflw run --runtime emulation` on a fixture with two levels of inputs, includes, multi-parent `extends` and `!reference`. A script asserting the interpolated and inherited values passes, and the same script with a wrong expected value fails.

## Known limitations (not in this PR)

- `rules:` on `include` entries are ignored; the file is always included.
- `trigger:` jobs run as no-op jobs locally.
- `default:` keyword values still aren't applied to jobs (pre-existing).

prs.title: fix(executor): evaluate job if: against real needs state
prs.body:
Follow-up to #126.

### Problem

#126 skipped jobs whose `needs:` did not succeed, but let any job with an explicit `if:` bypass the gate. That `if:` was then evaluated by `evaluate_job_condition` with `job_status` hardcoded to `"success"` and an empty `needs` context. After a failed need:

| `if:` | GitHub Actions | before this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `failure()` | runs | skipped |
| `success()` | skipped | ran |
| `always() && needs.x.result == 'failure'` | runs | skipped (`needs.x.result` was null) |
| `github.ref == '…'` (no status function) | skipped (implicit `success() &&`) | ran |

Jobs inside reusable workflows were not gated at all, because `run_called_workflow` runs its own batch loop.

### Change

The gate moves from the `execute_github_workflow` batch loop into `execute_job_with_matrix`, after the needs context is built:

- A job with no `if:` is evaluated as `success()`.
- An `if:` that calls none of `success()` / `failure()` / `always()` / `cancelled()` is evaluated as `success() && (<expr>)`. String literals and property names are ignored when looking for those calls.
- `success()` / `failure()` see the upstream status. It is `failure` when any transitive ancestor failed, which matches GitHub's documented ancestor rule. It is `skipped` when a direct need was skipped, so both functions are false.
- `needs.<id>.result` and `needs.<id>.outputs` are available to the job-level `if:`.
- - A matrix job's `needs.<id>.result` is the aggregate of its combinations: `failure` if any failed, otherwise `success` if any succeeded, otherwise `skipped`. It used to be whichever combination was recorded last. A combination that errors with `fail-fast: false` is now recorded as failed instead of dropped.
- Status-function detection uses the expression tokenizer instead of a separate scanner.
- A need with no recorded result does not block. That only happens for a matrix job that expanded to zero combinations. The old comment blamed `--target-job` plans, which always keep transitive deps.

Because `run_called_workflow` also runs jobs through `execute_job_with_matrix`, reusable workflows get the same rules. `job_blocked_by_needs` is removed, and the skipped `JobResult` literal is replaced by a `JobResult::skipped` constructor.

### Tests

Unit tests in `engine.rs` cover status-function detection, implicit `success()`, the skipped-need case and `upstream_status`. The existing `evaluate_job_condition` tests were moved to the new signature unchanged in meaning.

New integration tests in `needs_failure_propagation_test.rs`:

| test | asserts |
|---|---|
| `status_functions_see_the_failed_need` | `if: failure()` runs, `if: success()` skips |
| `needs_result_is_visible_to_job_if` | `needs.deploy.result == 'failure'` is true |
| `plain_if_is_still_gated_on_needs` | `if: ${{ true }}` still skips after a failed need |
| `need_skipped_by_its_own_if_skips_dependents` | `if: false` on a need skips its dependent |
| `any_failed_need_among_several_skips` | one failed need out of two skips |
| `ancestor_failure_propagates_past_an_always_job` | failed grandparent keeps `success()` false and `failure()` true |
| `reusable_workflow_jobs_skip_after_failed_need` | inner `needs:` chain is gated |
| `matrix_need_with_one_failed_combination_counts_as_failed` | plain, `failure()` and `needs.x.result` all see a failed matrix |
| `fail_fast_matrix_need_counts_as_failed` | fail-fast-skipped combinations don't mask the failure |
| `needs_outputs_are_visible_to_job_if` | `needs.<id>.outputs` drives a job `if:` both ways |
| `gate_skipped_need_reports_skipped_result` | a gate-skipped need reports `skipped` |

The integration test file is gated off Windows. It runs `bash` steps through the emulation runtime, and on `windows-latest` `bash` is the WSL launcher with no distribution installed, so every step fails. This was already failing on `main` since #126. The engine's own emulation unit tests use the same gate.

Against `main`'s engine, 5 of these fail. On this branch, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --tests -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --all-features` (836 passed) and `cargo check --no-default-features --workspace` are all clean.

### Behaviour change

Jobs with `if:` expressions that call no status function now skip after a failed need, as they do on GitHub. This is worth a line in the release notes.

prs.title: fix(executor): harden custom shell script path handling
prs.body:
Follow-up to #123, addressing the review findings left after merge.

### Fixes

- **Windows host + docker/podman.** The `{0}` script path was built with `guest_dir.join(name)`, which produces `/github/workflow\wrkflw-<uuid>` on a Windows host. A Linux container cannot resolve that. The guest path is now built as a POSIX string, the same way the `GITHUB_ENV` remap already does it. Windows CI did not catch this because the mock runtime resolves mounts with `Path::strip_prefix`, which accepts both separators on Windows.
- **Missing mount under a container runtime.** When `github_mount` was `None`, the code fell back to using `working_dir` as both host and guest path. That is only valid for host-side runtimes. Under docker/podman the step now fails with an explicit message instead of passing the container a host path. It is unreachable today because `GITHUB_ENV` is always seeded, but the invariant is now enforced instead of implied.

### Refactor

- The custom-shell setup moved out of `execute_step` into `prepare_custom_shell`. It returns a `CustomShellScript` guard whose `Drop` removes the script file, so cleanup happens on every exit path.
- The docker/podman check is now a single `uses_container_runtime` helper, stored on `StepContainerContext`. It was duplicated between `execute_step` and `prepare_container_mounts`.
- The resolved custom shell argv is logged at info level. The previous path was silent outside emulation's verbose logs.

### Tests

- `prepare_custom_shell_uses_posix_guest_path_under_container_runtime` asserts the guest path has no `\`, the script content is correct, and the file is removed on drop.
- `prepare_custom_shell_fails_without_github_mount_under_container_runtime` asserts the explicit failure and that nothing is written to the host.
- `prepare_custom_shell_rejects_missing_placeholder_without_writing` asserts no file is left behind on a validation failure.
- `custom_shell_resolves_relative_command_to_absolute_path` now uses a tempdir instead of writing its script into the crate directory.

`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features -- -D warnings`, `cargo check --no-default-features --workspace` and `cargo test --workspace --all-features` are clean locally on macOS.

### Not in scope

- The `cmd` arm still uses `cmd -c`. The real template is `cmd /D /E:ON /V:OFF /S /C "CALL "{0}""`, but it needs a Windows runner to verify.
